title: Adidas v. Puma: A Sibling Rivalry
summary: Josh and Chuck tell the story of Adidas and Puma, founded by feuding brothers Adolf "Adi" and Rudolf "Rudy" Dassler in Herzogenaurach (called "Hurtzo" in the episode), Bavaria. The episode covers their founding of Gebrüder Dassler shoe company around 1918, the 1928 and 1936 Olympics (including Jesse Owens), the brothers' split after World War II tensions (the bomb shelter incident and Adi's accusation that got Rudy arrested as a Gestapo suspect), the Dassler factory's wartime Panzerschreck production with forced French POW labor, the founding of Adidas and Puma, the town-wide rivalry (the "town of the lowered gaze"), Reebok, Nike, a listener mail about glass sponges from a marine PhD student, and Run-DMC's "My Adidas" endorsement deal.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about their footwear and a Hooters anecdote, then introduce the story of Adidas and Puma as a sibling rivalry.

segments.title: Dassler brothers found a shoe company in Herzogenaurach
segments.summary: Adi and Rudy Dassler begin cobbling athletic shoes in their mother's laundry in a Bavarian shoemaking town around 1918. Their company Gebrüder Dassler grows, their track spikes give sprinters traction, and Jesse Owens wears their shoes at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

segments.title: World War II and the Panzerschreck
segments.summary: The company's factory is conscripted for the war effort and produces the Panzerschreck, the German version of the American bazooka, in December 1943, using forced French POW labor.

segments.title: The brothers' feud and the bomb shelter incident
segments.summary: Tensions grow between Adi and Rudy and their wives after living together. During a Allied bombing, Adi's remark in the bomb shelter is taken by Rudy as an insult and becomes the final straw. Rudy is drafted, deserts, and is later arrested by the Allies after Adi reportedly accused him of being a Gestapo agent. Kata Dassler saves the factory from American soldiers.

segments.title: Founding of Adidas and Puma
segments.summary: The brothers split the company and found separate firms on opposite sides of the river. Adidas is named from Adi's name and Puma from Rudy's Ruda name. Adi focuses on technical quality while Rudy leads sales. Adidas leads Puma in revenue, and the brothers' mistakes, including Rudy's spat with a German national soccer coach and Adidas's 1954 World Cup stripes, are discussed, along with Reebok and Nike's rise.

segments.title: Town-wide rivalry and reconciliation
segments.summary: Herzogenaurach was split by the river, with families and workers divided between Adidas and Puma. Residents looked at each other's shoes, the mayor wore one of each brand's shoe in a 2009 friendly match, and the brothers never reconciled, with Rudy's late request to see Adi refused.

segments.title: Later history and Run-DMC
segments.summary: The families sold the companies in the late 1980s; Puma now owns Reebok and Gucci owns Puma. Frank Dassler works in Adidas legal. Run-DMC's 'My Adidas' and their 1986 Adidas endorsement deal, arranged after Angelo Anastasio saw fans holding up their shoes, launch hip hop shoe and sponsorship deals.

segments.title: Listener mail: glass sponges
segments.summary: A listener who is a marine PhD student describes sponges' role as possibly the earliest animals and their bioactive molecules for medicine, including an FDA-approved antiviral derived from a sponge.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and invite further emails and feedback.
